stages.title: CONCEPTUAL METHOD: WHAT PROBLEM IS BEING ASKED?
stages.terms: Major criticism: The problem of evil is not one argument but a family of challenges generated by the relation among a divine profile, the facts of suffering and wrongdoing, and norms governing what a good agent would permit.
stages.mechanism: Major criticism: The problem of evil is not one argument but a family of challenges generated by the relation among a divine profile, the facts of suffering and wrongdoing, and norms governing what a good agent would permit.
stages.trap: Major criticism: The problem of evil is not one argument but a family of challenges generated by the relation among a divine profile, the facts of suffering and wrongdoing, and norms governing what a good agent would permit.

stages.title: CLASSICAL FORMULATION AND MACKIE'S LOGICAL PROBLEM
stages.terms: Classical Formulation and Mackie's Logical Problem: Major criticism: The familiar questions - whether God is willing but unable, able but unwilling, or both able and willing while evil exists - are commonly labelled the Epicurean paradox.
stages.mechanism: The dilemma is transmitted in later discussion, prominently through Lactantius, and Hume's Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion gives a celebrated modern formulation through Philo.
stages.consequence: Therefore, if such a God exists, evil should not exist.
stages.trap: The exact popular wording should not be presented as a verbatim quotation from Epicurus.

stages.title: PLANTINGA'S FREE WILL DEFENCE
stages.terms: Plantinga's Free Will Defence: Major reply: The defence is strongest for moral evil.
stages.mechanism: If so, God's inability to actualize freedom-with-guaranteed-goodness is not lack of omnipotence, because the proposed object is not a feasible world God can strongly actualize.
stages.consequence: Therefore God's existence is logically compatible with moral evil.
stages.trap: If God causally determines every significantly free choice to be right, the choice is not libertarianly free in relation to God.

stages.title: EVIDENTIAL EVIL: ROWE, PROBABILITY AND SKEPTICAL THEISM
stages.terms: Recommended opening definition: Evidential force depends on a noseeum move: "We see no justifying reason; therefore there probably is none." Such reasoning is strong when observers would likely detect the relevant reason if it existed, as when looking for an elephant in a small room.
stages.mechanism: Recommended opening definition: Evidential force depends on a noseeum move: "We see no justifying reason; therefore there probably is none." Such reasoning is strong when observers would likely detect the relevant reason if it existed, as when looking for an elephant in a small room.
stages.consequence: Recommended opening definition: Evidential force depends on a noseeum move: "We see no justifying reason; therefore there probably is none." Such reasoning is strong when observers would likely detect the relevant reason if it existed, as when looking for an elephant in a small room.
stages.trap: The case is illustrative, not a claim that one event alone deductively disproves God.

stages.title: CLASSICAL THEODICIES AND DEFENCES
stages.terms: Classical Theodicies and Defences: Major reply: Created being is good insofar as it has being; evil is not a positive substance made by God but a privation, corruption or disorder of a due good.
stages.mechanism: Major reply: Created being is good insofar as it has being; evil is not a positive substance made by God but a privation, corruption or disorder of a due good.
stages.consequence: Hick contrasts a soul-making world with a hedonistic paradise that continuously adjusts to desire.
stages.trap: Major reply: Created being is good insofar as it has being; evil is not a positive substance made by God but a privation, corruption or disorder of a due good.

stages.title: NON-CLASSICAL THEISMS AND REVISED DIVINE ATTRIBUTES
stages.terms: Non-Classical Theisms and Revised Divine Attributes: Recommended opening definition: Whitehead is the metaphysical source; Hartshorne argues against classical omnipotence; David Ray Griffin develops process theodicy; John Cobb systematizes process theology.
stages.mechanism: Recommended opening definition: Whitehead is the metaphysical source; Hartshorne argues against classical omnipotence; David Ray Griffin develops process theodicy; John Cobb systematizes process theology.
stages.trap: [THESIS] Process thought does not preserve classical unilateral omnipotence.

stages.title: EXISTENTIAL EVIL, PROTEST AND HORRENDOUS EVILS
stages.terms: Recommended opening definition: Existential approaches ask not only whether a proposition is coherent but what stance is humanly and morally possible before suffering.
stages.mechanism: Dostoevsky's Ivan Karamazov refuses a final harmony purchased through innocent suffering.
stages.trap: Recommended opening definition: Existential approaches ask not only whether a proposition is coherent but what stance is humanly and morally possible before suffering.

stages.title: INDIAN AND NON-WESTERN FRAMEWORKS
stages.terms: Indian and Non-Western Frameworks: High-value transition: Karma (morally consequential action) is structurally strong on distribution but morally dangerous when converted into retrospective certainty about a victim.
stages.mechanism: Recommended opening definition: Indian traditions do not share one answer because they disagree about creator, self, world, karma (morally consequential action) and liberation.
stages.consequence: [ARGUMENT] Action produces a causal potency or karmic consequence; continuity across lives widens the field in which consequences mature; present suffering may therefore be connected to prior agency; liberation ends bondage or the production of future consequences.
stages.trap: Recommended opening definition: Indian traditions do not share one answer because they disagree about creator, self, world, karma (morally consequential action) and liberation.

stages.title: HARD CASES AND META-LEVEL CRITIQUES
stages.terms: Hard Cases and Meta-Level Critiques: High-value transition: Animal suffering is a central evidential challenge because predation, disease, parasitism and extinction precede human agency and often seem unrelated to moral growth.
stages.mechanism: High-value transition: Animal suffering is a central evidential challenge because predation, disease, parasitism and extinction precede human agency and often seem unrelated to moral growth.
stages.consequence: Recommended opening definition: Animal suffering is a central evidential challenge because predation, disease, parasitism and extinction precede human agency and often seem unrelated to moral growth.
stages.trap: Stable-law and evolutionary accounts explain mechanisms and goods such as complex life, but not obviously the intensity and duration of sentient pain.

stages.title: COMPARATIVE SYNTHESIS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS
stages.terms: Comparative Synthesis and Practical Implications: Final verdict: Comparison is strongest when each position is judged through the same axes of ultimate reality, world relation, human relation, causation and religious function.
stages.mechanism: Final verdict: Comparison is strongest when each position is judged through the same axes of ultimate reality, world relation, human relation, causation and religious function.
stages.consequence: High-value transition: Theodicies should be compared through the divine attribute revised, the evil explained, the residual case and the moral cost of the explanation.
stages.trap: Add one Indian comparison that changes the frame rather than decorating the answer.
